name: Dodge Charger Daytona
hook: In March 1970 one of these became the first car ever to lap a closed course at more than 200 mph.
story: Talladega, September 1969. The speedway was brand new, the banking was savage, and tyres were shredding in practice. Most of the star drivers packed up and went home. Richard Brickhouse stayed. Chrysler handed him a winged Charger Daytona built for somebody else, and he led 33 laps to the flag. It was the only win of his career, on the car's first day out. Six months later Buddy Baker took a Daytona around that same track at 200.447 mph. Nobody had ever lapped a closed circuit at 200 before. The steel nose cone and that absurd wing were doing exactly what the engineers had promised: about 1,200 pounds of downforce pressing on the front, 600 more on the back. Then Chrysler's winged cars won 33 of the 48 races run in 1970. NASCAR answered by capping aero cars at 305 cubic inches, and the Daytona was done. Eighteen months, start to finish. It was legislated out of existence rather than beaten.
description: The Charger Daytona is a 1969 Dodge Charger rebuilt for superspeedways. It wears an 18-inch steel nose cone, a flush rear window, and a 23-inch rear wing carried on two tall struts. NASCAR required 500 road-going copies before the shape could race, so Dodge built 503 and sold them through dealers. Most carried the 375 hp 440 Magnum; roughly 70 got the 426 Hemi. It remains the most extreme body NASCAR ever allowed on a stock car.
